title: Configure notification schemes
content:
Jira apps can generate email notifications for various events that happen throughout the lifecycle of a work item, including custom events. Notifications are defined within a notification scheme (see below), which associates particular events with particular email recipients. The notification scheme is then assigned to a particular space.
You can use the same notification scheme for more than one space.
Jira apps are pre-packaged with a notification scheme called Default Notification Scheme. This scheme is associated with all new spaces by default. However, you can disassociate this notification scheme from the space via the Space Summary page, as described below. You can also modify this scheme or if you prefer, create other notification schemes for particular spaces.
Create a notification scheme
- Select Settings (), then Work items.
- Select Notification schemes to open the notification schemes page.
- Select the Add notification scheme button.
- On the Add notification scheme page, enter a name for the notification scheme and a short description of the scheme.
- Select Add. The Edit Notifications page appears. This is where you can add notifications/recipients as described below.
Notification scheme save in real time. When you're finished, you can simply navigate away from the screen.
After you've created your scheme, you need to associate it to the spaces that you want to use the scheme as described below.
Add an event recipient to a notification scheme
To add a new recipient for a particular event to a notification scheme, you need to:
- Identify the notification scheme used by the relevant space.
- Add that recipient to the appropriate event in this notification scheme.
To add a new recipient for a particular event:
- Select Settings (), then Work items.
- Select Notification schemes to open the notification schemes page, which lists all the current notification schemes in your Jira installation.
- Locate the notification scheme of interest and click its linked name to open the Edit Notifications page for that notification scheme. 
The Edit Notifications page lists all of the events , along with the recipients who will receive notifications when each event occurs.
- Select the Add link in the appropriate event row (see the list of events below), which opens the Add Notification page, where you can choose who to notify (about the event) from the list of available recipients (see below).
- Select the appropriate recipient (filling in any required information for your particular choice of recipient).
- Select the Add button. You are taken back to the Edit Notifications page (see above), with the notification you just specified now listed against the appropriate work item event.
- If you make a mistake, or you would like to remove who is being notified, simply click the Delete link beside the person/group/role.
Associate a notification scheme with a space or space board
Now that the scheme is created, you can associate the scheme with the spaces that you want to use it. Once associated, any events on that space or its board will trigger the notifications that you configured in the scheme.
To associate a notification scheme to a space (and its board):
- Select Settings (), then Spaces.
- Search for and select the space you want to associate the notification scheme with.
- Next to the name of your space in the sidebar, select More actions (•••), then Space settings.
- Select Notifications.
- Select the Actions dropdown menu and choose Use a different scheme.
- On the subsequent Associate Notification Scheme to Space page, which lists all available notification schemes, select the notification scheme you want to associate with the space and select the Associate button.
Events
Jira apps support the following events, which can generate email notifications (as defined in a notification scheme).
| Event | Description | 
|---|---|
| Work item created | A work item has been entered into the system. | 
| Work item updated | A work item has had its details changed. This includes the deletion of a work item comment. | 
| Work item assigned | A work item has been assigned to a new user. | 
| Work item resolved | A work item has been resolved (usually after being worked on and fixed). | 
| Work item closed | A work item has been closed (note that a work item may be closed without being resolved). | 
| Work item commented | A work item has had a comment added to it. | 
| Work item comment edited | A work item's comment has been modified. | 
| Work item reopened | A work item has been re-opened. | 
| Work item deleted | A work item has been deleted. | 
| Work item moved | A work item has been moved into or out of this space. | 
| Work logged on work item | A work item has had hours logged against it (i.e. a worklog has been added). | 
| Work started on work item | The Assignee has started working on a work item. | 
| Work stopped on work item | The Assignee has stopped working on a work item. | 
| Work item worklog updated | An entry in a work item's worklog has been modified. | 
| Work item worklog deleted | An entry in a work item's worklog has been deleted. | 
| Generic event | The exact nature of this event depends on the workflow transition(s) from it was fired. | 
| Custom event(s) | The exact nature of these events depends on the workflow transition(s) from which they were fired. | 
Jira apps don’t have a specific notification event for the deletion of work item comments. When a work item's comment is deleted, Jira sends out an email notification as an 'Work item updated' event.
Recipients
The following types of recipients can receive email notifications.
| Recipient | Description | 
|---|---|
| Current assignee | The user to whom the work item is currently assigned. | 
| Reporter | The user who originally created the work item. | 
| Current user | The user who performed the action that has triggered this event. | 
| Space owner | The user who is managing the space to which the work item belongs. | 
| Component lead | The user who is managing the component to which the work item belongs. | 
| Single user | A particular user in your Jira system. | 
| Group | A particular group in your Jira system. | 
| Space role | The members of a particular space role for this space. We recommend using space roles (rather than groups) in your notifications as this can help minimize the number of notification schemes in your system. How to manage space roles | 
| All watchers | All users who are "watching" the work item, the people listed in the Watchers field. | 
| User custom field value | The value of a custom field of type User Picker or Multi User Picker that may have been associated with work items. An example of where this can be useful: if you have a custom User field called Tester, you can have the tester notified when a work item is resolved. | 
| Group custom field value | The value of a custom field of type Group Picker or Multi Group Picker that may have been associated with work items. | 
User control over email notifications
Each user on your Jira Cloud site (including you) can choose to turn off email notifications for certain situations, to reduce the amount of email they get from Jira. For example, they can configure their personal settings to get an email when someone mentions them but not for activity on work items where they're the reporter.
By default, they'll get email updates for work item activity when:
- They’re watching the work item
- They’re the reporter
- They’re the assignee for the work item
- Someone mentions them
If they don't want email updates for any of those situations, they can uncheck the relevant checkbox. For example, if they only want emails when someone mentions them, they should uncheck all the checkboxes apart from the Someone mentions you checkbox.
Email notifications will only be sent to people who have permission to view the relevant work item — that is, people who:
- have the Browse Spaces permission for the space to which the work item belongs; and
- are members of any work item security levels that have been applied to the work item.
Jira can only send email notifications if SMTP email has been enabled (see Configuring email notifications).
Jira's default setting is to not notify users of their own changes. This can be changed on a per user basis via their profile preferences.
Customize the look and feel of your email notifications
Currently, Jira Cloud does not offer a way for you to customize the look and feel of your email notifications. But, there are many third party apps available on the Atlassian Marketplace that can help you.
